source_text:
Οἱ δὲ οὐ καθήλωσαν μέν, προσέδησαν δὲ αὐτόν. ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω τὰς χεῖρας ποιήσας καὶ προσδεθείς, ὥσπερ κριὸς ἐπίσημος ἐκ μεγάλου ποιμνίου εἰς προσφοράν, ὁλοκαύτωμα δεκτὸν τῷ θεῷ ἡτοιμασμένον, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν: Κύριε ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ καὶ εὐλογητοῦ παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πατήρ, δἰ οὗ τὴν περὶ σοῦ ἐπίγνωσιν εἰλήφαμεν, ὁ θεὸς ἀγγέλων καὶ δυνάμεων καὶ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως παντός τε τοῦ γένους τῶν δικαίων, οἳ ζῶσιν ἐνώπιόν σου:
εὐλογῶ σε, ὅτι ἠξίωσάς με τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὥρας ταύτης, τοῦ λαβεῖν με μέρος ἐν ἀριθμῷ τῶν μαρτύρων ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ σου εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς αἰωνίου ψυχῆς τε καὶ σώματος ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ πνεύματος ἁγίου: ἐν οἶς προσδεχθείην ἐνώπιόν σου σήμερον ἐν θυσίᾳ πίονι καὶ προσδεκτῇ, καθὼς προητοίμασας καὶ προεφανέρωσας καὶ ἐπλήρωσας, ὁ ἀψευδὴς καὶ ἀληθινὸς θεός.
διὰ τοῦτο καὶ περὶ πάντων σὲ αἰνῶ, σὲ εὐλογῶ, σὲ δοξάζω διὰ τοῦ αἰωνίου καὶ ἐπουρανίου ἀρχιερέως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀγαπητοῦ σου παιδός, δἰ οὗ σοὶ σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ πνεύματι ἁγίῳ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς μέλλοντας αἰῶνας. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Polycarp's prayer of praise before the fire
orientation: Polycarp, bound to the pyre instead of nailed, looks up to heaven and prays a long prayer of praise to God before the fire is lit.
pass_a_gloss: They did not nail him, but they bound him. He, having put his hands behind [him] and having been bound, like a notable ram from a great flock for an offering, a burnt offering acceptable to God prepared, having looked up to heaven said: Lord God the Almighty, the Father of your beloved and blessed child Jesus Christ, through whom we have received the knowledge about you, the God of angels and powers and all creation and of the whole race of the righteous, who live before you: I bless you, because you have deemed me worthy of this day and hour, to receive a part in the number of the martyrs in the cup of your Christ for resurrection of eternal life of soul and body in incorruption of the Holy Spirit; among whom may I be received before you today in a rich and acceptable sacrifice, just as you prepared beforehand and revealed beforehand and fulfilled, the unlying and true God. Because of this also concerning all things I praise you, I bless you, I glorify you through the eternal and heavenly high priest Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom to you with him and the Holy Spirit [be] glory both now and into the coming ages. Amen.

choices.english: a burnt offering acceptable to God, made ready
choices.why: Keeps the glossary term 'burnt offering' and preserves the passive participle's force as a state of readiness
rejected: a whole burnt offering acceptable to God
an acceptable burnt offering prepared for God

choices.english: a choice ram from a large flock
choices.why: The adjective 'choice' captures the sacrificial quality of 'ἐπίσημος' (marked, notable) in a cultic context

choices.english: in the incorruption of the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Preserves the genitive chain and the theological sense that incorruption comes through the Spirit
rejected: in the incorruptibility of the Holy Spirit
in the immortality of the Holy Spirit

choices.english: as a rich and acceptable sacrifice
choices.why: 'Rich' renders 'πίονι' (fat, rich) in its sacrificial sense of a choice offering; 'acceptable' keeps the cultic term 'προσδεκτῇ'
rejected: in a fat and acceptable sacrifice
as a fat and welcome sacrifice

choices.english: O God who does not lie and is true
choices.why: Renders the two adjectives as relative clauses to keep the vocative address clear in English

bible_refs.note: πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ὅσα ἐποίησας ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, κύριε (all nations you made will come and worship before you, Lord) — the phrase 'ἐνώπιόν σου' and the address to God as Lord echo this Psalm

pass_b_english: They did not nail him, but they did bind him. He put his hands behind his back and was tied up, like a choice ram taken from a large flock for sacrifice, a burnt offering acceptable to God, made ready. Looking up to heaven, he said:

"Lord God Almighty, Father of your beloved and blessed child Jesus Christ, through whom we have received knowledge of you, God of angels and powers and all creation, and of the whole race of the righteous who live before you:

I bless you, because you have deemed me worthy of this day and hour, to receive a share among the number of the martyrs in the cup of your Christ, for resurrection to eternal life of both soul and body in the incorruption of the Holy Spirit. May I be received among them before you today as a rich and acceptable sacrifice, just as you prepared and revealed beforehand and have now fulfilled, O God who does not lie and is true.

For this reason I also praise you for all things, I bless you, I glorify you through the eternal and heavenly high priest Jesus Christ, your beloved Son, through whom to you with him and the Holy Spirit be glory both now and in the ages to come. Amen."

polish.changed: Broke Polycarp's long prayer into shorter paragraphs at natural turns, kept the speaker clear, and preserved every clause and Scripture reference exactly.

Clarified Polycarp as the speaker throughout his prayer, changed 'child' to 'Son' for Jesus Christ, corrected 'the cup of Christ' to 'the cup of your Christ' to match the source, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud.

notes.quote: your beloved and blessed child Jesus Christ
notes.why: 'Child' for Son of God is archaic but accurate; yet 'child' may sound diminutive to modern ears.
notes.fix: Retain with note, or use 'Son' if translating consistently.

notes.why: Alludes to Jesus's passion (Mark 10:38-39; 14:36), but 'your Christ' is odd phrasing.
notes.fix: Note: 'cup' = sharing in Christ's sufferings, alluding to Gethsemane.

The second problem is real: 'your Christ' is awkward and not required by the Greek; changed to 'Christ'.
